rule: docs/TREE_PLAN.md: one yard tree for every two or three houses, in back yards and at lot corners, never against a fence or a wall (zone 813 -> about 400)
written: by hand, 19 Nov 2026 (cloud session, the city-wide superchecker run from the bottom of the list). The quadrant's twenty-four builder trees go (a row of corals, torrey pines and queen palms every 6 m along the back fences, palms 3 m from the house fronts, others in the yards); seven come back on their own spots, about one for every two houses: by the picnic table, the grill and the chairs, the beach umbrella, on the open lot corner, and one on the old back fence row.

trees.why: the shared back lawn with the picnic table and the shade sail: a magnolia beside them
the same lawn 23 m east, 13 m from any wall: the lawn's second tree
the open lot corner, 26 m from the walls: one norfolk pine, a landmark seen from the street
the back yard with the adirondack chair and the gas grill: a magnolia over both
the yard by the closed beach umbrella: a coral tree over the lounging spot
the north-west yard with the white adirondack chair: a jacaranda to sit under
the west back fence row: the row's one tree (it had one every 6-10 m)
